title: Canary psychometrics and A/B ethnography scratchpad (wip)
content:
Purpose:
This scratchpad collects experiments and heuristics that combine quantitative canary signals with lightweight qualitative / ethnographic checks. The idea: add human-centric signal probes (micro-surveys, conversation sampling, steward interviews) to complement numeric SLOs when rolling out LLM-powered features.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: product owners, rollout stewards, SRE oncall, solutions eng, CS triage.
- Scope: mid-to-large canaries for generation and reranking features where user experience quality is nuanced and not fully captured by token-level metrics. Not for infra-only changes (use standard infra runbooks).

Why this feels distinct:
- Many rollouts hit a blind spot where latency/cost are stable but output quality subtly degrades (tone shift, hallucination modes, policy edge-case regressions). Quant metrics miss human perception and edge-case harms until they accumulate.
- We want a compact, repeatable layering of psychometric probes + ethnographic sampling that fits into our existing canary lifecycle.

High-level pattern (one-paragraph):
- During canary exposure, run usual telemetry (latency, error rates, model-specific metrics). In parallel, deploy a 3-part human-probing pipeline: 1) short in-product micro-survey (1–2 questions) routed to sampled users; 2) automated conversation sampling that surfaces 50 high-risk responses/day to a steward queue; 3) structured steward interviews (daily stand with CS/product) to capture qualitative themes and emergent failure modes. Combine these signals in a lightweight risk score that can trigger throttles, rollback, or expanded exposure.

Signal matrix (examples we should capture):
- Quantitative: token latency p95, tail latency (reqs > 1s), error rate (%), model divergence score vs baseline (BLEU-like embedding similarity), cost per 1k tokens.
- Psychometric: 1–5 satisfaction prompt mean + trend, negative sentiment rate (NLP classifier), clarity rating (user-reported), trust indicator (yes/no).
- Ethnographic: steward severity counts (0–5), emergent theme tags (privacy, hallucination, safety, offensive), exemplar response IDs.

Trigger heuristics (proposal, tuned per product):
- Immediate throttle/limit exposure if: latency p99 increases > 2x baseline OR error rate spikes > 0.5 percentage points AND steward severity >= 2.
- Soft rollback (pause roll forward + auto-alert) if: negative sentiment lift > 2 sigma over 72h OR micro-survey NPS drop >= 1.2 points AND at least 10 steward-flagged exemplars.
- Hard rollback if: any confirmed P0 safety incident OR automated policy-violation classifier triggers on > 5 unique user responses with steward confirmation.

Operational checklist (canary owner):
- Pre-launch (48–24h): define hypothesis, define micro-survey text, register steward roster, set sampling rates, add experiment tag to telemetry dashboards, create Slack channel #canary-{name}.
- Day 0 (first exposure): smoke run on synthetic traffic for 30m, sanity-check micro-survey flow (send to internal test cohort), confirm steward queue connectivity (Sentry/Linear integration), verify cost guardrails.
- Daily cadence (during exposure): morning steward triage (15m), review top 50 steward-sampled responses, run quick thematic synthesis, update risk score, communicate to stakeholders.
- Post-mortem (within 3 business days of finish): narrative + exemplar corpus + decisions log (why we kept/rolled back), add lessons to experiment library.

Sampling plan (practical defaults):
- Micro-survey: 0.5% of traffic for high-sensitivity features, 0.1% for low-sensitivity. Keep survey length <= 2 questions. Rotate phrasing every experiment to avoid bias.
- Conversation sampling: deterministic stratified sampling across user regions and request types; prioritize queries containing policy keywords or rare entity patterns.
- Steward queue: cap 100 items/day per steward, auto-deprioritize items older than 72h if not actioned (but keep archive).

Roles & responsibilities (quick map):
- Canary owner: defines hypothesis, coordinates micro-survey, authorizes exposure changes.
- Steward(s): triage sampled responses, tag themes, escalate P0 incidents.
- SRE/infra: verify latency/capacity telemetry; ready to throttle traffic or scale pools.
- CS/solutions: surface early customer reports and add qualitative context.
- Legal/security: on-call if privacy or compliance flags appear.

Steward triage guide (short):
- Triage tags: hallucination, harmful-content, private-data-leak, incoherent, hallucinated-facts, hallucinated-legal, bias.
- Severity rubric: 0 = ok, 1 = annoyance, 2 = usability regression, 3 = repeated harmful outputs or customer complaint, 4 = clear policy violation, 5 = P0 safety incident.
- Actions: severity >= 3 -> immediate Slack alert to #canary-{name}-ops + create ticket with exemplar and steps to reproduce.

Quick rollback playbook (1-min to read):
- Step 0: Canary owner verifies signals and steward confirmations.
- Step 1: Set traffic weight to 0% for experiment variant via console (or disable flag).
- Step 2: Re-route traffic to baseline model variant (model pin) and confirm request flow is healthy.
- Step 3: Run targeted query set (30 s) to verify no recurring failure.
- Step 4: Create incident record, tag stakeholders, schedule deep-dive.

Lightweight evaluation artifacts (what to capture):
- 20 exemplar pairs (input + baseline output + experiment output), steward notes, micro-survey raw responses, timeline of signal deltas, cost delta.

Open questions / areas for follow-up:
- How to automate psychometric baseline comparison across models? (embedding-based similarity + calibration set?)
- Minimum steward staffing for different exposure sizes (0.5% vs 5%).
- Privacy guardrails for storing sampled responses (anonymization and retention).
- Integration with rollout console: small UX idea to show "qualitative pulse" next to latency and cost.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Prototype micro-survey wording and instrument in test org - owner: Ethan.
- Wire up a steward queue in Linear for one active canary and test notification flows - owner: Samir.
- Draft retention/anonymization rules with Security - owner: María.

Notes to self (fragmented):
- keep survey neutral phrasing, avoid leading text.
- consider rotating steward reviewers to avoid annotation drift.
- instrument per-route sampling in console (feature request).

References and footprints:
- link to existing experiment-runbook (see linked_artifacts).
- sketch of dashboard idea: small panel showing psychometric trend + top tags.

Unresolved items for product review meeting:
- threshold numbers for "soft rollback" need numerical tuning per product. Suggest running synthetic experiments to calibrate.
- decide whether steward tags map to formal taxonomy (yes/no).

End of scratchpad - use this as a basis for a more structured playbook once we validate with 2 real canaries.

(Author notes: heuristic-first, fairly opinionated. This doc expects iteration; keep it in drive and mark final when we codify runbook templates and console integration.)
